doc.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004

title: Radio play, the Internet and file trading
summary: The band falls between straight-ahead jazz and smooth jazz formats, getting only occasional public radio play. Fleck sees free trading as a problem and expects home recording to matter more than major labels.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Just to wrap up, you had mentioned that you guys don’t get radio play, which is sort of distressing but I’m wondering is it because people have a hard time defining what you do?

Yeah. Like for instance if you’ve got a straight ahead jazz show we’re too something, we’re not a straight ahead jazz group. And if you have a contemporary jazz show that tends to be smooth jazz, we’re not smooth jazz so that knocks us out of jazz play unless you just have college or more occasional stations that do more unusual programming. And we get played on some of those. Or then NPR occasionally. But again, where is the broad heading that every town has that kind of station and you’re on it regularly? That doesn’t happen. Bluegrass shows play some of my stuff. But you know it’s more of a public radio type inconsistent airplay thing. It’s not that we don’t get played at all but it’s not a big factor. It’s not like if you had a hit single or something, that nothing like that has happened since the very beginning.
The Internet’s probably been helpful to your band.

Probably. But although some people feel like the trading of the records has been harmful to the records that you put money into that are not paid off, are being traded for free. That’s a problem we’re all dealing with that I don’t really know what the answer is to.
The cat’s out of the bag on that one.

Yeah. And that’s why making them at home is a big deal and why being on major label may not make sense in a few years. Getting a big budget for a record that’s going to get pirated and traded for free is going to be hard for them to justify after a while unless some solution comes up.
